main_text.head: CAP. VI.
De explicatione loci difficilis ad regiam potestatem pertinentis. I. Sam.8.
main_text.p: {a}IUdicibus sæcularibus in Imperio Iu-daico succesferunt Ecclesiastici, qui & Iudices fuerunt simul & Sacerdotes: inter hos cùm Samuel suos filios substi-tuisset, vers. 3. Qui non ambulaverunt in viis ejus, sed declinaverunt post avaritiam, ac-ceperuntq; munera, & perverterunt judi-cium: congregati universi majores natu Israel, venerunt ad Samuelem, dixerunt-que ei, vers. 5. Ecce tu senuisti, & filij tui non ambulant in viis tuis, constitue nobis Regē

page.notes: The Greek line in the first quotation is only partly legible; its letters are marked illegible. The Greek word "Κλῦειν" is read with doubt for the accent. The reference mark on "prudentissimus" is read as "z". The left-hand fragments are cut off by the scan edge and are given only as the visible line ends. The first word's large initial is printed as I with V for the vowel u; read as IUdicibus. The mark "{a}" in the text is printed as a superscript a; the mark letters are as printed. The note "vers. 3." and "vers. 5." are right-margin notes.
